newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold tests fresh lows, eyes downside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold tests fresh lows, eyes downside.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold was probing fresh low ground on Wednesday amid fresh producer selling and dealers said prices would probably continue drifting still lower in the near term.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) were under light pressure from news Russia would resume shipments to Japan around July 10.
GOLD - Prices were hovering around the $332.00 support level early on Wednesday, having come under pressure from producer hedging in Asian trading hours, European dealers said.
"The reason gold is lower this morning is Australian producer selling, and there was quite a lot of it," a dealer said.
"There was some support from physical offtake but there's no reason for prices not to go still lower."
Despite the overwhelmingly bearish charts and market sentiment, prices were more likely to drift down rather then plummet, dealers said.
"There's no panic. I don't see a dramatic plunge," the dealer added.
Critical support was seen at $325.10 an ounce, the point low from 1993.
Technical analysts noted, however, that technical indicators were moving into oversold territory. Gold's 14-day RSI was indicated at 30 on Wednesday morning.

"With the technical indicators drifting sideways close to the oversold band, expect a period of consolidation around $335.00," said analyst William Adams of brokers Rudolf Wolff, referring to Comex August gold.
"In the longer term, look to a minimum target of $330.00/1.00, the downside potential of the descending triangle which commenced on May 12," he added.
Spot gold was indicated at $332.20/$332.60 at 0730 GMT after closing at $333.40/$333.90 in London on Tuesday.
SILVER - The most stable of the precious metals at the moment was finding good support at $4.60 an ounce.
But against the background of a declining gold price, silver was unlikely to find many takers on the upside, dealers said.
It was last at $4.64/$4.66, down two cents.
PLATINUM/PALLADIUM - News that long-delayed Russian PGM supplies could resume by July 10 had put a little pressure on the market but a sharp price drop was unlikely, dealers said.
"Supplies have been delayed for six months and it will take a long time for the situation to normalise," a dealer said.
Russia's PGM export agency informed Japanese clients by fax that Russia would resume PGM shipments to Japan around July 10, Japanese precious metals traders said.
At 0730 GMT platinum was at $427.00/$432.00 versus $440.50/$445.50, while palladium was at $189.00/$194.00 compared with $194.00/$199.00.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
